pages.title: History about NACOSTI
pages.intro: NACOSTI is Kenya's apex national institution responsible for coordinating, regulating, advising and promoting science, technology and innovation.

sections.title: Origins and Evolution
sections.body: The Commission traces its history to the National Council for Science and Technology (NCST), established under the Science and Technology Act Cap 250 of 1977. NCST laid the groundwork for Kenya's national scientific infrastructure and research advisory mechanisms.

sections.title: Establishment under STI Act 2013
sections.body: In 2013, the enactment of the Science, Technology and Innovation Act No. 28 transformed NCST into the National Commission for Science, Technology and Innovation (NACOSTI), granting modern regulatory, coordination, and quality assurance powers.

sections.title: Our Role Today
sections.body: NACOSTI assures quality in research, advises national and county governments on STI matters, coordinates national research priorities, and spearheads Kenya's transition into an innovation-driven knowledge economy.

pages.title: Mandate & Functions
pages.intro: The Commission's statutory mandate is to regulate and assure quality in the science, technology and innovation sector and advise the Government in matters related thereto.

sections.title: Core Functions
sections.body: Under Section 6 of the STI Act No. 28 of 2013, NACOSTI develops national STI priorities, registers research institutions, licenses research activities, and accredits Institutional Scientific and Ethics Review Committees (ISERCs).

sections.title: Coordination and Promotion
sections.body: The Commission coordinates multi-agency research programs, monitors STI mainstreaming across Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs), and champions public awareness of science and technology.

sections.title: Socio-Economic Value
sections.body: By assuring research integrity and ethical standards, NACOSTI safeguards the Kenyan public, protects research participants, and aligns scientific innovation with national development goals.

pages.title: Vision, Mission & Core Values
pages.intro: NACOSTI is committed to leadership, integrity, and excellence in guiding Kenya's national science, technology, and innovation ecosystem.

sections.title: Vision
sections.body: A globally competitive science, technology and innovation system for sustainable development.

sections.title: Mission
sections.body: To facilitate, coordinate, regulate and assure quality in science, technology and innovation through policy leadership, research coordination, and multi-sectoral collaboration.

sections.title: Core Values
sections.body: Integrity, Professionalism, Excellence, Inclusivity, Accountability, and Customer-Centric Service Delivery guide all decisions and operations of the Commission.

pages.title: Quality Policy
pages.intro: NACOSTI is committed to delivering consistent, impartial, transparent and continually improving regulatory and advisory services to the scientific and research community.

sections.title: Quality Commitment
sections.body: The Commission maintains a Quality Management System aligned with international standards (ISO 9001:2015), ensuring that regulatory, licensing, accreditation, and advisory services meet statutory and customer requirements.

sections.title: Continual Improvement
sections.body: We review our operational processes regularly through internal quality audits, risk assessments, and stakeholder feedback to enhance institutional effectiveness and service delivery.

pages.title: Corporate Objectives
pages.intro: NACOSTI's corporate objectives translate the statutory mandate into concrete strategic goals and measurable performance indicators.

sections.title: Strategic Regulation and Quality Assurance
sections.body: To enhance efficiency and transparency in research licensing, ethical clearance accreditation, and institutional registration across Kenya.

sections.title: Evidence-Based Advisory Leadership
sections.body: To generate policy advisories and scientific intelligence that inform national development plans, Vision 2030, and county development frameworks.

sections.title: Institutional Strengthening
sections.body: To optimize organizational capacity, digital infrastructure, financial sustainability, and human resource competencies for world-class public service.

pages.title: Board of the Commission
pages.intro: The Board of Commissioners provides strategic governance, policy leadership, and fiduciary oversight for NACOSTI.

sections.title: Governance Mandate
sections.body: Appointed pursuant to Section 4 of the STI Act No. 28 of 2013, the Board is responsible for policy direction, strategic resource allocation, institutional risk management, and overall stewardship of Kenya's STI regulatory framework.

sections.title: Board Composition and Committees
sections.body: The Board comprises distinguished Kenyan scientists, academic leaders, private sector innovators, and key government representatives. Governance is executed through specialized committees including Audit & Risk, Strategy & Finance, and Technical & Quality Assurance.

pages.title: Management
pages.intro: The executive management team is responsible for operationalizing Commission policies and driving day-to-day regulatory and advisory excellence.

sections.title: Executive Leadership
sections.body: Headed by the Director General and Chief Executive Officer, the management team executes the Board's strategic priorities, ensures regulatory compliance, and oversees public service delivery across all directorates.

sections.title: Cross-Directorate Execution
sections.body: Management coordinates the Directorates of Research Accreditation & Quality Assurance, Scheduled Sciences, and Corporate Services to assure integrated performance and timely response to stakeholder needs.

pages.title: CEO's Corner
pages.intro: Perspectives, strategic priorities, and communiqués from the Director General / CEO of NACOSTI.

sections.title: A Word from the Director General
sections.body: Science, technology, and innovation are the indispensable engines of sustainable national prosperity. NACOSTI is steadfast in creating an enabling regulatory environment that safeguards ethics while accelerating discovery, technology diffusion, and industrial commercialization.

sections.title: Strategic Focus Areas
sections.body: Our current focus centers on digital modernization of licensing systems, expanding research funding partnerships, mainstreaming emerging technologies like artificial intelligence and biotechnology, and inspiring the next generation of STEM researchers.

pages.title: Research, Accreditation & Quality Assurance
pages.intro: The Directorate ensures the integrity, safety, and quality of all scientific research conducted within the borders of Kenya.

sections.title: Mandate and Responsibilities
sections.body: Oversees the administration of the Research Information Management System (RIMS), issues research licenses, registers public and private research institutions, and accredits Institutional Scientific and Ethics Review Committees (ISERCs).

sections.title: Quality Assurance and Compliance Audits
sections.body: Conducts post-licensing monitoring, institutional inspections, and bioethics compliance evaluations to ensure that research adheres strictly to statutory protocols and international ethical standards.

pages.title: Scheduled Sciences
pages.intro: The Directorate coordinates scientific disciplines to drive technological progress and evidence-based policy formulation.

sections.title: Disciplines Covered
sections.body: Coordinates programs and scientific panels across Agricultural & Natural Sciences, Physical & Industrial Sciences, Health Sciences, and Humanities & Social Sciences.

sections.title: Scientific Advisories and Priority Setting
sections.body: Engages scientific communities, analyzes sectoral data, and formulates technical advisories that guide the national research agenda and address pressing socio-economic challenges.

pages.title: Corporate Services
pages.intro: The Directorate provides institutional, financial, legal, and operational infrastructure to support the Commission's mandate.

sections.title: Core Departments
sections.body: Encompasses Human Resource Management, Finance and Accounting, Information and Communication Technology (ICT), Supply Chain Management, Legal Services, and Corporate Communications.

sections.title: Service Standards and Governance
sections.body: Ensures prudent stewardship of public resources, compliance with public financial laws, robust digital infrastructure, and adherence to the NACOSTI Service Charter.

pages.title: Advisory
pages.intro: Providing high-level policy guidance and scientific intelligence to the National Government, County Governments, and the public.

sections.title: Statutory Advisory Role
sections.body: Pursuant to the STI Act 2013, NACOSTI advises government ministries and regional administrations on national science priorities, STI investments, and technological readiness.

sections.title: Evidence-Based Policy Development
sections.body: Produces policy briefs, national research reports, and technical forecasts to guide national legislation, economic planning, and emergency preparedness.

pages.title: Collaborations and Partnership
pages.intro: Fostering strategic alliances with regional and international science organizations to advance Kenya's STI capacity.

sections.title: International Scientific Diplomacy
sections.body: NACOSTI serves as Kenya's liaison and focal point for major global scientific treaties and bodies, including the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), International Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology (ICGEB), and the Biological Weapons Convention (BWC).

sections.title: Regional Alliances and Research Consortia
sections.body: Collaborates with the East African Science and Technology Commission (EASTECO), the African Union, and bilateral research councils to unlock collaborative grants, cross-border research, and talent exchange.

pages.title: Research Licensing
pages.intro: All researchers, institutions, and scholars seeking to conduct research in Kenya must obtain a statutory Research License.

sections.title: Mandatory Legal Requirement
sections.body: Under Section 12 of the STI Act No. 28 of 2013, conducting research in Kenya without a valid license issued by NACOSTI is an offence punishable by law.

sections.title: Application via RIMS
sections.body: Applications are submitted entirely online via the Research Information Management System (RIMS). Applicants submit research proposals, institutional endorsement letters, and ethical review approvals.

sections.title: Processing Timelines and Support
sections.body: Applications undergo thorough peer review and administrative assessment, with processed licenses issued digitally upon approval and fee verification.

pages.title: Registration of Research Institutions
pages.intro: Formal statutory registration and certification of public and private research institutions operating in Kenya.

sections.title: Regulatory Framework
sections.body: Sections 16 to 22 of the STI Act 2013 require every institution intending to undertake research in Kenya to be formally registered by NACOSTI.

sections.title: Evaluation Criteria
sections.body: Institutions are evaluated on governance frameworks, qualified human resources, physical laboratory infrastructure, safety standards, and institutional financial sustainability.

pages.title: Accreditation of ISERCs
pages.intro: Accrediting and overseeing Institutional Scientific and Ethics Review Committees (ISERCs) across Kenya.

sections.title: Ethics Oversight
sections.body: NACOSTI accredits institutional ethics committees to review and approve research proposals involving human subjects, animal models, or sensitive environmental ecosystems.

sections.title: Standards and Annual Audits
sections.body: Accredited ISERCs must adhere to national bioethics guidelines, maintain diverse committee composition, and submit annual performance and monitoring reports to NACOSTI.

pages.title: Accredited ISERCs in Kenya
pages.intro: Official directory of NACOSTI-accredited Institutional Scientific and Ethics Review Committees.

sections.title: Accredited Committees Directory
sections.body: A curated roster of approved ethics review committees situated in universities, research institutes, hospitals, and specialized public health agencies.

sections.title: Jurisdiction and Validation
sections.body: Researchers must submit protocols to accredited ISERCs with corresponding jurisdiction before seeking national licensing from NACOSTI.

pages.title: Accreditation of Research Institutions
pages.intro: Formal peer assessment recognizing research institutions that maintain exceptional standards of scientific quality.

sections.title: Accreditation Standards
sections.body: Rigorous evaluation assessing research governance, laboratory calibration, peer-reviewed outputs, researcher credentials, and safety standards.

sections.title: Institutional Recognition
sections.body: Accredited status grants formal recognition of technical competence, enhances international funding eligibility, and assures collaborative partners of research excellence.

pages.title: National Scientific & Ethics Review System (NSERS)
pages.intro: An integrated national digital portal connecting researchers, ethics review committees, and the Commission.

sections.title: Digital Review Workflow
sections.body: NSERS automates the submission, tracking, peer review, and clearance of ethical research protocols across Kenya.

sections.title: Efficiency and Oversight
sections.body: Reduces review turnaround times, eliminates duplication of submissions, and provides the Commission with real-time oversight of national bioethics compliance.

sections.title: Strategic Reports and Publications

sections.title: About ICGEB and NACOSTI's Role
sections.body: NACOSTI is the National Liaison Office for the International Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology (ICGEB), facilitating Kenyan scholars' participation in international research.

sections.title: Available Programs
sections.body: Kenyan researchers and postgraduate students are eligible to apply for Arturo Falaschi fellowships, early-career grants, and sponsored scientific courses globally.

sections.title: Employment at NACOSTI
sections.body: NACOSTI is an equal opportunity employer that values competence, diversity, and dedication to national service. Vacancies are advertised openly in the national press and on this portal.

sections.title: Internships and Attachment Opportunities
sections.body: The Commission provides structured industrial attachment opportunities for undergraduate students and paid graduate internships to develop national capacity in STI management.

pages.intro: Find answers to common questions regarding research licensing, institutional registration, ethics review, and NACOSTI services.

pages.title: Science, Technology and Innovation Act No. 28 of 2013
pages.intro: The principal legislation governing the promotion, coordination and regulation of science, technology and innovation in Kenya.

sections.title: Statutory Foundations
sections.body: Enacted to facilitate the promotion, coordination and regulation of the progress of science, technology and innovation in Kenya, and to assign priority to the development of STI.

sections.title: Key Institutional Mandates
sections.body: Established NACOSTI as the regulator, the National Research Fund (NRF) to finance research, and the Kenya National Innovation Agency (KeNIA) to promote commercialization.

pages.title: Research Licensing Fees
pages.intro: Schedule of statutory fees for research licensing applications in Kenya.

sections.title: Prescribed Fee Structure
sections.body: Prescribed by the Science, Technology and Innovation Regulations, differentiating between Kenyan citizens, East African Community residents, and non-citizens across academic and commercial categories.

sections.title: Payment Channels
sections.body: Payments must be made through official government payment channels, including eCitizen and authorized Commission accounts, with automated receipt issuance.
